days.title: London to York — the East Coast racer
days.summary: Out of King's Cross on the fastest rails in Britain — cathedral country to York, the railway city, for the Minster and the great museum.

stops.name: London King's Cross — boarding
stops.blurb: Under the great twin arches where the East Coast expresses have left for Scotland since 1852.

stops.name: York Minster & the walls
stops.blurb: North Europe's largest Gothic cathedral above medieval streets — an evening walk on the city walls.

stops.name: York — railway-hotel night
stops.blurb: A grand Victorian railway hotel beside the station — and the National Railway Museum next door for the morning.

days.title: York to Edinburgh — castles and the sea
days.summary: Durham's cathedral on its rock, the Northumberland coast at the window, over the Royal Border Bridge into Edinburgh.

stops.name: Durham — cathedral on the rock
stops.blurb: The Norman cathedral and castle rise over the Wear — the finest view from any railway in England.

stops.name: The Northumberland coast
stops.blurb: Castles and cold blue sea — Alnmouth, Bamburgh's outline, Holy Island across the sands.

stops.name: Edinburgh — under the Castle
stops.blurb: Waverley station sits in the garden valley below the Castle rock — the Old Town rises straight from the platform ends.

days.title: Edinburgh to Fort William — the West Highland Line
days.summary: Across to Glasgow and up the most scenic railway in Britain — lochside, moor and mountain to the foot of Ben Nevis.

stops.name: Glasgow — a Highland breakfast
stops.blurb: Queen Street station and a proper breakfast before the line turns north along the Clyde.

stops.name: Rannoch Moor — the empty miles
stops.blurb: The line floats on brushwood across a wilderness no road crosses — deer on the moor, weather rolling in.

stops.name: Fort William — beneath Ben Nevis
stops.blurb: The Highland junction town under Britain's highest mountain — sleeper carriages idle at the platform.

days.title: The steam finale — Fort William to Mallaig
days.summary: The Jacobite steam train over the Glenfinnan Viaduct to the silver sands and the fishing quay at Mallaig, the Hebrides across the water.

stops.name: Glenfinnan Viaduct
stops.blurb: Twenty-one arches curving above the glen with Loch Shiel beyond — steam, whistle and the most famous railway view in the world.

stops.name: The silver sands of Morar
stops.blurb: White shell-sand bays and turquoise water — the Hebridean light at the carriage window.

stops.name: Mallaig — journey's end
stops.blurb: The rails end at the harbour wall: landed prawns on the quay, the Isle of Skye across the Sound.
